# #1995: Patch: the AI weighs the countdowns on the board, its own as a payoff and the enemy's as a threat
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Jlockeed's Supply Drop says "in 3 turns, deal 4 damage to each enemy" (or hand out Radiant cards). The practice AI almost never casts it, because it looks only one turn ahead and never sees the payoff. When a player casts it against the AI, the countdown badge is plain on the board, yet the AI keeps putting small units in front of a blast that will kill them. After this the AI counts what a countdown will do, discounted for the turns still to wait. It casts Supply Drop when that is worth it, and it holds units back from a blast it can see coming. Stinkyscape's planned "in N turns" cards will need the same.

## Why

- **The sweeps.** Supply Drop (Meditative+ #4) is flagged `neverPlayed` in pass 1 at both tiers (`training/history/sweep-2026-10-25-2.md:38-39`). In pass 2 it is played 8 times in 167 affordable turns at Easy and 6 in 196 at Hard (`:222-223`; `sweep-2026-10-22.md` shows the same). Over that report's 188 pass-2 rows, the median at-risk card is played on 19.7% of its affordable turns (recomputed from the report for this suggestion).
- **The evaluation.** It prices no unmarked delayed effect (`crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs:307-313`: "nor does an unmarked delayed effect"). Nothing in `crates/ai` reads a delayed effect's `due_own_turn` or its badge `label` (`crates/engine/src/state.rs:747-757`, R1181000).
- **The reply.** It scores a line at the seat's next decision, so a payoff two or more turns out is never seen.
- **Tests.** The AI's Meditative+ tests check only that the play is legal (`crates/ai/tests/ai/meditative_plus.rs`).

## Proposal

- Score a line that arms a countdown a second time, and every finalist while a countdown is on the board. The second score runs on a copy whose countdowns come due at their owner's next turn start, so the existing reply step fires them through `reduce`.
- Blend the two scores by a named per-turn share raised to the turns left, in `crates/ai/src/config.rs`.
- Only the public badge's entry is read (R169, R185), so nothing hidden reaches the AI.
- No engine change.

## Where it lands

- `crates/ai/src/reply.rs`, `crates/ai/src/simulate.rs` or `evaluate.rs`, `crates/ai/src/config.rs`
- `crates/ai/tests/ai/meditative_plus.rs`, `crates/ai/README.md`
- §9.9's Evaluation paragraph in `spec/09-architecture.md`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Holding Supply Drop with 2 mana against three 3-health enemy units and no better play, the AI casts it in Combat mode. This test fails today.
- [ ] Facing an enemy Combat countdown due next turn, the AI scores putting a 3-health unit down below holding it, other things equal.
- [ ] With no countdown on the board, every decision is as before: the puzzles, pinned positions and fixture smokes are unchanged.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh sweep meditativeplus-004` shows plays in pass 1 at both tiers, and the timing gate is green.

## Size and risks

Hard (AI): about 5 files and about 250 lines. Firing the countdown on today's board can overstate its kills, which the discount tempers. It costs one more reply per countdown line, inside the node budget.
